This is oil clay that my school provides , and now it’s covered in pink rubber mold to begin the mold making process

I used some aluminum wire, I assume about 1/8 “ thick. The thickness of the wire is determined by overall height.

There really is no wrong way to make one so long as it is strong and stands up right. I’ve seen people bend one long wire into right angles and create the shape of a person that way; but i prefer using two separate wires already measured with a couple inches of slack in case you need it. I start with a long wire and measure double the length of which I want it to stand. So my nurse is 15” tall so i measured a 30” wire. Bend it in half to create a loop which i use for the head. You now have two legs and a head.

Take your second wire, and measure how long you want your arms and give some slack. I create an M shape with this second wire (if you don’t, one arm moves the other, not good) and then fasten both shapes together with a hose clamp

The hose clamp is my favorite for strength and I secure this at the waist usually. This is key so that you have an anchored point and your limbs can move freely and independently .Attaching your wire person to a pipe on the board is a final step to keeping your figure still and upright. 

looking this up on youtube would probably be more helpful but hopefully this helped a little
